summary:
Martian Atlas is an interactive, layered web application built to help future explorers and rovers plan safe Martian treks across Jezero Crater while conducting science along the way.

Today, portals like NASA Mars Trek and PDS hold rich data across separate missions, forcing specialists to cross-reference layers manually, while onboard AutoNav only avoids rocks locally.

Our solution unifies multi-mission NASA and USGS open data into a single survival map, combining HiRISE orbital imagery, MOLA/HRSC elevation models, 21 real Perseverance science sample sites, and 325 cataloged surface hazards rated 1–5 in criticality. Using an A* pathfinding engine over a 50 m terrain-cost grid, Martian Atlas automatically computes up to three safe multi-stop routes (fastest, shortest, least exposed) and dynamically recalculates detours in real time, whenever explorers report new obstacles along the trail.

Project -> https://github.com/Sl3nc/Martian_Atlas
details:
WHAT IT DOES & HOW IT WORKS

Martian Atlas is a web-based layered GIS and route-planning system for Jezero Crater (approx. 26 x 24 km, bounds 77.152°–77.612° E, 18.289°–18.688° N), built to help explorers and rovers plan safe Martian treks while visiting high-priority science targets.

  1. Multi-Mission ETL Pipeline (325 Hazards and 21 Science Samples):
  • In-Situ Telemetry: We extracted 708 real Perseverance stops from NASA MMGIS (M20_waypoints.json) and filtered waypoints where the rover IMU recorded chassis tilt of 8.0° or higher, identifying 315 real terrain hazards (rough terrain for 8°–15° and steep slope for 15° or above).
  • Orbital Mapping: Because rover logs only show where the rover could drive, we mapped 10 major blocking zones from USGS, HiRISE, and AI4Mars data, including craters (Belva, Santa Cruz, Lahontan), sand traps (Seitah North and South), steep scarps (Cape Nukshak 28°, Kodiak Butte 32°), and boulder fields.
  • Science Along the Way: Integrated 21 real Perseverance sample sites with Sol metadata and raw camera photos, plus 22 illustrative Hazcam scenes matched to hazard criticality levels (1 to 5).
  1. 50 m Terrain Cost Grid and 8-Connected A* Routing:
  • Jezero Crater is modeled as a 518 x 474 grid of 50 m x 50 m cells over the USGS HRSC-MOLA Digital Elevation Model (DEM).
  • Impassable hazards block cells within their radius plus a criticality safety buffer (10 m at level 1 up to 50 m at level 5). Passable hazards increase traversal cost (1 + 4 * severity). Terrain slope penalizes climbs and strictly blocks any slope above 25°.
  • An 8-connected A* algorithm with line-of-sight smoothing computes the safest path across Origin, Science Waypoints, and Destination, generating up to 3 distinct route alternatives (fastest, shortest, and least exposed) while discarding candidates with more than 60% overlap.
  1. Live Traverse Simulation and "Waze-Style" Rerouting:
  • Explorers can view interactive topographic elevation and slope profiles and simulate a live traverse (estimating drive hours and Martian Sols based on a ~150 m/h speed and 4.5 hours per Sol).
  • If an explorer reports a surprise obstacle (criticality 1 to 5) on the map, the cost grid updates immediately and A* recalculates a safe detour in real time from the current position.

HOW OUR PROJECT IS CREATIVE

During the hackathon, we validated our concept with a NASA mentor on Space Apps Connect (Discussion #2168: https://github.com/nasa/spaceapps/discussions/2168). The mentor confirmed a key gap: NASA Mars Trek visualizes orbital layers and onboard AutoNav avoids rocks locally, but no single public system combines a structured historical obstacle database with automated route planning.

  • "Waze for Mars": Martian Atlas pioneers collaborative, real-time hazard logging paired with multi-objective A* routing and scientific waypoint planning.
  • Tactical GPS Export: Beyond the web app, we processed a 25 GB HiRISE mosaic and a 1.8 GB DEM in QGIS to export georeferenced tactical maps with World Files (.pgw / .wld) ready for external GPS hardware.

BENEFITS & INTENDED IMPACT

  • For Mission Planners and Future Astronauts: Eliminates slow, error-prone manual cross-referencing across separate NASA portals. When planning a Marswalk to collect samples near hazardous dunes like Seitah or steep delta scarps, explorers instantly get three risk-scored routes and automatic detours around newly discovered hazards.
  • For Science and Education: Turns complex planetary datasets (PDS, MMGIS, MOLA, HiRISE) into an intuitive, interactive survival guide that inspires students and citizen scientists to explore Mars safely.

FACTORS CONSIDERED BY OUR TEAM

  • Scientific and Physical Validity: Equirectangular projection at Jezero's standard parallel (18.4663° N), strict 25° maximum safe slope threshold, criticality-based safety buffers (10–50 m), and realistic Martian Sol operational windows.
  • Usability, Performance, and Accessibility: Built with zero external runtime dependencies for fast loading, keyboard navigation, ARIA attributes, high-contrast visual legends, and localStorage persistence.

TOOLS, CODING LANGUAGES & SOFTWARE USED

  • Frontend and Routing Engine: Vanilla JavaScript (ES Modules), HTML5 Canvas, CSS3.
  • Dev Server and Automated Verification: Node.js 20+ (node:test suite with 20 automated tests verifying geo-projection, cost grid, A*, and dynamic rerouting).
  • ETL and Image Processing (Offline): Python (pandas for telemetry and hazard ETL; OpenCV with SIFT feature matching and Pillow for coordinate registration and image conversion).
  • GIS and Cartography: QGIS (3D DEM modeling, hillshade analysis, raster pyramid optimization, layer blending of USGS HRSC-MOLA DEM and HiRISE orthomosaics, and .pgw World File georeferencing).
